## T282 — two follow-ups on T278's commit wrapper Both defects fixed; all controls PASS (wrapper regression 9/9, hook regression 6/6, T280's regression-precommit.sh still 3/3). ### Defect 1 — false FAIL on an already-committed path (tools/git-commit-mine) **Root cause.** The verify-after step only asked "is the named path in the new commit?". A path whose content was already committed by an earlier commit is NOT in the new commit (there was nothing to commit for it), so the wrapper reported `FAIL — commit does not contain: ` on a healthy commit — reproduced: mixed invocation (new + already-committed path) committed the new file correctly and then cried FAIL; the pure already-committed case exited 2 "REFUSED — nothing staged". **Fix — three cases distinguished in verify-after:** 1. path IS in the new commit → committed by this invocation (success); 2. path not in commit but `git cat-file -e HEAD:

` succeeds AND `git diff --quiet HEAD --

` is clean → already committed and unchanged — reported as a note ("nothing to commit for these"), NOT a failure; 3. anything else → genuinely missing — the real FAIL. Plus the empty-staged branch: when `git add` stages nothing and every named path is already committed and unchanged, exit 0 with "OK — nothing to commit: already committed and unchanged" instead of the old refusal. The `cat-file -e` guard is required: `git diff --quiet HEAD -- ` returns 0 (nothing to compare), so diff-alone would misclassify a missing path as case 2. **Candour — case 3 has no seeded control.** A genuinely-missing path is nearly unreachable through the wrapper's own flow: a nonexistent path fails at `git add` ("pathspec did not match", exit 2), an ignored path fails at `git add`, and any staged path lands in the commit. Case 3 survives as a safety net for races (a file modified between `git add` and `git commit` by another console). The wrapper's known-bad is still the T268 foreign-staged refusal (arms 2/4/9); arms 6-7 are the null controls for this fix. ### Defect 2 — staged-path subset backstop (tools/hooks/pre-commit, gate 2) New gate running BEFORE claimlint (cheaper, and the refusal is the relevant one when a foreign path is staged): staged paths must be a subset of the committing task's declared deliverables ∪ its findings files (`findings/-*.json`) ∪ the two fleet-coordination surfaces (CURRENT.md, HANDOVER.md). **One implementation, two callers.** The wrapper's scope resolution (kanban lookup + deliverables= parsing + findings glob + surfaces) moved verbatim into the new `tools/git-commit-mine-lib.sh`; the wrapper sources it, the hook calls it. A second copy of the parsing is how the two would drift apart and the hook would start refusing the wrapper's own commits. The wrapper's five T278 arms still pass unchanged. **Rulings (explicit, per the brief):** - identity known (MANAGENT_TASK_ID set by bin/subagent) + out-of-scope staged path → **REFUSE** (exit 1), naming each path, with the T268-incident remedy (never unstage another console's work; commit through the wrapper; --no-verify only after reviewing the paths yourself). - identity ABSENT (human commit, court seat) → **warn-and-allow with the paths listed**. Refusing every unlabelled commit would wedge the Orchestrator (which caused incident 2). - identity set but unresolvable (kanban read failed / task absent) → **warn-and-allow with the paths listed** — identity unknown = unlabelled; refusing would wedge a worker whose kanban is momentarily unreadable. - wrapper `--explicit` commit (the wrapper now exports GIT_MINE_EXPLICIT=1) → **warn-and-allow with the paths listed** — the wrapper took responsibility on the way in. Without this channel, an explicit-mode commit with foreign staged content (the Orchestrator's designed mode) would be refused by the hook: a false positive on the seat that caused incident 2. - No new env-var escape hatch beyond --no-verify (documented in the refusal message) — T278's warning that escape hatches are the rot point. MANAGENT_STORE is honored by the hook (scratch-kanban substrate isolation, src/managent/main.zig:150) so the backstop is testable without touching the live kanban; the wrapper also passes it through to the lib (default unchanged, so wrapper behavior is byte-identical in the tested arms). ### Controls - `tools/regression-git-commit-mine.sh` — now 9 arms: T278's 5 (all still PASS) + arm 6 (already-committed alone → clean no-op, RC=0), arm 7 (mixed → commit contains exactly the new path, no FAIL), arm 8 (task identity via kanban — previously UNTESTED, T278 only exercised --bundle mode), arm 9 (task identity + out-of-scope path → refused naming it). - `tools/regression-git-commit-mine-hook.sh` (new) — 6 arms: null in-scope allow; seeded foreign staged → REFUSED naming the path (T268 fixture shape); unlabelled → warn-and-allow naming it; explicit → warn-and-allow; unresolvable identity → warn-and-allow listing paths; findings-glob staged file → allowed. - `sh tools/regression-precommit.sh` (T280's) — all three checks still pass (installed-ness, null, seeded). - End-to-end: real `git commit` in a scratch repo with the hook installed — bypass attempt (MANAGENT_TASK_ID set, foreign staged) REFUSED naming the foreign path, commit aborted, staged content intact; unlabelled commit warned-and-allowed. ### Observed but not acted on - A worker could pass `--explicit` routinely to dodge both the wrapper's scope check and the hook — but --explicit was already a full escape from the wrapper's scope check, so the hook matching that design is consistent; closing it would need an escape-hatch-free redesign and is a policy call for the Orchestrator. - `git show --name-only` lists deleted paths, so a deletion commit passes case 1 (verified empirically) — deletions of in-scope paths are legitimately allowed by both gates. - The live repo carried unstaged modifications from other consoles (docs/infra/managent/*, src/managent/main.zig) during this task; commits name only T282's own paths.
